newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Phone strike delays Tel Aviv stock trading.
newsitem.headline: Phone strike delays Tel Aviv stock trading.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Tuesday delayed its main trading of Mishtanim and Maof stocks as a strike by Bezeq Israel Telecom workers created communications problems, a bourse spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said brokerage houses and banks could not get through to the bourse so they decided not to have trading.

The morning session of call market trading known as the Meretz took place as usual. The Meretz session determines the market trend and executes small orders while the bulk of trading in the 100 most liquid stocks takes place in the later session known as the Mishtanim.

The spokeswoman said the bourse would issue a statement shortly regarding trading for the rest of the day. She did not know if trading would resume following a labour court's ruling this morning that Bezeq workers must end their week-long strike.
Bezeq union chief Shlomo Kfir said workers' representatives would meet soon to decide whether to abide by the court's decision.
The strike over government plans to privatise more of the company has curtailed telephone repair and operator information services.
